item.title: Suffrajitsu!!!!
item.description: May Whitley demonstrating grappling techniques shared with suffragettes in their fights with men and the cops. There were other suffragettes that trained judo/jiujitsu as well such as Edith Garrud, but I have not found existing video footage of her. Also a great example of a man, Charles Cawkell, being the lovely (silent) assistant to Whitley, leading the demonstration. He was a judo black belt in the UK, and assisted in sharing grappling techniques. The film is a short film titled The Weaker Sex! (Sayeth thou!!) From 1933.

item.title: Dissection of Flock Safety Camera
item.description:
Note that the version dissected is an older version and the modem is no longer being sold.
After opening the Flock Safety camera, the biggest item is the PHD Energy rechargeable lithium ion battery
NimbeLink Skywire LTE cellular modem inside Flock Safety camera
Lantronix SD624 Audio Kit SOM inside Flock Safety camera
Taoglas AP.17E GPS module inside Flock Safety camera
LEDs and motion detection sensor in Flock Safety camera
Another view of LEDs and motion detection sensor in Flock Safety camera
5MP 16mm Fixed M12 1/2 Inch IR Filter Action Camera Lens in Flock Safety camera
https://www.cehrp.org/dissection-of-flock-safety-camera/ Back of Flock Safety camera showing antenna connector for cellular modem and connector for solar panel Here’s the list of component parts that we were able to identify: Cellular: NimbeLink Skywire LTE modem – FCC ID N7NHL7648 P/N: NL-SW-LTE-S7648 (https://nimbelink.com/products/4g-lte-cat-1-att-sierra-wireless/) Battery: PHD Energy lithium ion rechargeable – 10.8V, 19Ah, 205.2Wh SD624 Audio Kit SOM (https://www.lantronix.com/products/open-q-624a-development-kit/) Wifi/bluetooth: LITE ON Technology WCBN3510A 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac 2T2R+BT V4.2LE GPS: Taoglas AP.17E – one stage 17mm active patch antenna Module (https://www.taoglas.com/product/ap-17e-gps-1-stage-active-patch-17mm-2/) Camera lens: 5MP Action Camera Lens 16mm Fixed M12 1/2 Inch IR Filter Updated July 12, 2026, with a link to GitHub code for a newer version of a Flock camera: https://github.com/kernelstub/FlockCamRE
